title: Multi Class Classification Quiz
description: Test your understanding of multi class classification

questions.question: What is the main challenge in multi-class classification compared to binary classification?
options: Multi-class problems always have more data
Most fundamental algorithms are designed for binary classification
Multi-class problems are always more complex
questions.explanation: Most fundamental classification algorithms like logistic regression and SVM are inherently binary classifiers, so we need strategies to extend them to handle multiple classes.

questions.question: In the One-vs-Rest (OvR) strategy, how many binary classifiers are trained for a problem with 5 classes?
questions.explanation: One-vs-Rest trains exactly one binary classifier for each class, so for 5 classes, we train 5 binary classifiers (Class 1 vs Rest, Class 2 vs Rest, etc.).

questions.question: How does One-vs-Rest make predictions on new data?
options: It randomly selects one of the trained classifiers
It averages the outputs of all classifiers
It selects the class whose classifier gives the highest confidence score
It uses majority voting among all classifiers
questions.explanation: OvR runs all binary classifiers on the new instance and selects the class whose classifier produces the highest confidence score or probability.

questions.question: What is a key advantage of One-vs-Rest over One-vs-One for problems with many classes?
options: OvR requires fewer binary classifiers to train
questions.explanation: OvR trains K classifiers for K classes, while One-vs-One trains K(K-1)/2 classifiers. For many classes, OvR requires significantly fewer classifiers.

questions.question: In One-vs-Rest, what labels are used when training the binary classifier for Class 2?
options: 1 for Class 2, 0 for Class 1, -1 for all other classes
1 for Class 2, 0 for all other classes
2 for Class 2, 1 for all other classes
1 for Class 2, 2 for all other classes
questions.explanation: When training the binary classifier for Class 2, we assign label 1 to all Class 2 instances and label 0 to all instances from other classes.

questions.question: What is a potential issue with One-vs-Rest when classes are highly imbalanced?
options: Binary classifiers may be biased toward the majority class
questions.explanation: When classes are imbalanced, each binary classifier sees mostly negative examples (all other classes), which can bias the classifier toward predicting the negative class.

questions.question: Which evaluation metric is most appropriate for assessing overall performance in multi-class classification?
questions.explanation: A confusion matrix shows detailed performance across all classes, while macro-averaged F1-score provides a single metric that accounts for performance on all classes equally.

questions.question: What happens if no binary classifier predicts positive for a new instance in One-vs-Rest?
options: The algorithm fails and returns an error
The class with the highest score (even if negative) is selected
The most frequent class from training is selected
questions.explanation: Even if all classifiers predict negative, we still select the class whose classifier gives the highest score, as this represents the 'least negative' or most likely class.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a common application of multi-class classification?
options: Medical diagnosis with multiple possible conditions
questions.explanation: Predicting house prices is a regression problem (predicting continuous values), not a classification problem (predicting discrete categories).

questions.question: What is the main benefit of using regularization in One-vs-Rest classifiers?
options: It prevents overfitting in individual binary classifiers
questions.explanation: Regularization (L1 or L2) helps prevent overfitting by penalizing large weights in each binary classifier, leading to better generalization on new data.
